senses.definition: A clasp or fastening used to fasten a cope in the front, usually decorative.

quotes.text: The morse bore a seraph's head in gold-thread raised work.
quotes.reference: 1891, Oscar Wilde, chapter XI, in The Picture of Dorian Gray, London; New York, N.Y.: Ward Lock & Co., →OCLC:

quotes.text: The morse is said to roar or bellow loudly, but the animal we slew made no outcry, [...]
quotes.reference: 1829, [Robert Pearse Gillies], “The Voyage. (Continued.)”, in Tales of a Voyager to the Arctic Ocean. […] (Second Series), volume III, London: Henry Colburn, […], →OCLC, page 66:

quotes.text: Then we passed through a great deale of small ice, and sawe, upon some peices, two morses, and upon some, one; and also diuers seales, layeing upon peices of ice.
quotes.reference: 1880, Clements R Markham, editor, The Voyages of William Baffin, 1612-1622, published 1881:
